name: Everest Kanto Cylinders Ltd
tagline: High-pressure cylinders leader, 50%+ India market share, tailwinds in CNG & hydrogen
verdict_headline: Well-positioned market leader with 26% ROCE, cheap valuation (P/E 8.9x), execution-dependent upside
verdict_reasoning: Rank 1 in Confluence-100 mechanical scoring (strongest non-large-cap candidate)
Conviction upgraded to MEDIUM (four-box score 3.0, up from 2.5; moat/tailwind/TAM upgraded from weak)
26% ROCE leader with >50% India market share, 48-year operational heritage, 30M+ cylinders installed
Capex pipeline credible: Egypt online May 2026, Mundra +15% capacity, US Type-4 expansion $50-75M order backlog
Valuation deeply discounted: P/E 8.9x for 26% ROCE business (market pays 15-20x for quality), 51% upside to analyst target (161 INR)
Near-term risk: Q1 FY27 showed cyclical headwind (revenue -10%, EBITDA -23%), working capital drain during growth phase, execution on capex timelines

Bull case: If Egypt/Mundra/US execute, margins recover to 15-17% guidance, CNG infrastructure accelerates, multiple re-rates to 12-15x = 3-4x price × 3-5 year 10-15% PAT CAGR = potential 10x in 3-5 years
Bear case: CNG demand remains cyclical (petrol/diesel price gap closure), competitive threat (Supreme Industries Type-4), capex delays/cost overruns, working capital drag persists
business_overview: EKC is India's largest manufacturer of high-pressure seamless gas cylinders (>50% market share, 30M+ in service globally). Founded 1978, established technical/regulatory moats. Core: CNG cylinders for automotive, industrial gas storage (O2, N2, Ar, He), medical applications. Expanding: semiconductors, defence, hydrogen Type-4. Global footprint: 6 plants (Tarapur, Kandla, Mundra greenfield, Dubai, Pittsburgh USA, Egypt online May 2026). FY25: Rs 1,499 cr revenue (+22.6% YoY), Rs 179 cr EBITDA (12%), Rs 98 cr PAT. ROCE 26%, P/E 8.9x. Analyst targets 109-161 INR (7.5-51.7% upside). Capex pipeline: Mundra +15% capacity, Egypt regional hub, US Type-4 expansion ($50-75M backlog). FY27 guidance: 15-20% growth, 15-17% EBITDA margin.

q1_fy27.note: Temporary supply constraints; organic PAT down ~25% after adjusting for Q1 FY26 ERC gain

fundamentals_narrative: Revenue recovery in FY25 (+22.6%) after FY23-24 trough driven by CNG price normalization and US subsidiary (CP Industries) turnaround (+42% to Rs 374 cr). India standalone strong at Rs 946 cr (+22.6%). EBITDA margins recovering but not regaining FY21-22 levels (12% vs 17% peak), reflecting commodity pricing pressure and mix challenges. However, management guidance of 15-17% sustainable margin suggests pricing power improving in higher-value segments (CV CNG revival, semiconductors, defence). Q1 FY27 saw temporary headwind (supply-side constraints) but EBITDA margin expanded to 14% (best since FY26 Q3 16%), indicating underlying strength as supply normalizes. ROCE of 26% is durable and well above market average, suggesting competitive moat. Key watch: Working capital management (FY25 CFO collapsed to Rs 58 cr despite higher profit due to inventory/receivables surge) and capex execution (Egypt/Mundra on-track timelines).
technical_read: Declining trend to Oct 2025 (high 163 INR Apr 2025, current 102 INR) reflects Q1 weakness and market concerns over cyclical CNG demand, capex-funded borrowing, and working capital drain. Volume consolidating near 102 INR. On recovery (Egypt online, margin guidance proof), potential 109-161 INR analyst targets suggest 7-58% upside range. 30-week EMA and support levels should anchor position if headlines support.
sentiment_summary: Mixed-to-Cautious: ValuePickr forum shows long-standing bull thesis (Dec 2021 post, 89k views, strong conviction from RajeevJ on >50% market share and 40% capacity expansion), but recent EquityEdge research (Feb 2026) calls out margin pressure post-FY22 super-cycle, working capital headwinds, and structural EV risk to LCV segment. Q1 FY27 weakness created near-term caution. Catalysts (Egypt online, margin guidance proof, US order ramp) could re-ignite bull narrative if executed.
community_signal: ValuePickr forum: Long-standing bull thesis from Dec 2021, refreshed with detailed quarterly analysis (EquityEdge Feb 2026 premium research). Cited strengths: 50%+ market share, 40%+ capacity expansion (Mundra), CNG tailwind, high-pressure cylinder moat. Cited concerns: Cyclicality, margin reset post FY22 super-cycle, EV penetration in LCV segment, capex execution risk. Overall: Institutional conviction strong, retail interest moderate.
bse_notes: BSE Code 532684, NSE Code EKC. Liquidity moderate (ADTV ~Rs 15-20 cr). Promoter holding ~55-60%, institutional/retail ~20-25%. Dividend payout sporadic (nil in recent years due to capex reinvestment). No major corporate actions pending beyond capex announcements.
bull_case: 1) Market leader with 50%+ India share, 26% ROCE (vs 12-15% market avg) = quality business attracting premium valuation. 2) Tailwinds real: CNG infrastructure expanding in India (govt fuel transition policy), hydrogen adoption accelerating (12.1% CAGR global), semiconductors/defence growing in India. 3) Capex pipeline credible: Egypt online May 2026 (Rs 50-60 cr Y1 revenue), Mundra +15% capacity (CNG revival support), US Type-4 expansion ($50-75M order backlog, Rs 100 cr FY28 revenue target). 4) Management execution proven: Egypt greenfield on track, US turnaround achieved, survived FY23 CNG shock. 5) Valuation attractive: P/E 8.9x for 26% ROCE (market pays 15-20x for quality), 51% upside to 161 INR target, potential 3-4x multiple re-rating if margins recover to 15-17% guidance + revenue CAGR 10-15% = 10x in 3-5 years. 6) Small-cap optionality: If hydrogen adoption accelerates and EKC Type-4 R&D succeeds, new market opens (100x scenario, low probability but non-zero).
bear_case: 1) Cyclical demand: CNG cylinders sensitive to pump pricing arbitrage. If petrol/diesel prices rise or CNG prices stabilize, CV CNG demand could weaken (e.g., FY23 CNG doubled to Rs 80/kg, crushed demand). Revenue volatility high (FY22 +79%, FY23 -44%). 2) Q1 FY27 weakness signals execution or demand headwinds: -10% revenue, -23% EBITDA YoY. If temporary, recovers; if structural, thesis at risk. 3) Working capital drag: FY25 CFO collapsed to Rs 58 cr despite higher profit (massive -Rs 97 cr WC swing on inventory/receivables). Growth is consuming cash, raising refinancing risk if operations worsen. 4) Competitive threat: Supreme Industries entering Type-4 composites (structural advantage vs steel), slow market shift away from EKC's core (steel cylinders). 5) Capex execution risk: Egypt/Mundra/US timelines could slip, cost overruns possible (greenfield projects). Capex not yet generating returns (multi-year payback 18-25 years for Egypt greenfield). 6) EV penetration in LCV segment: Long-term, electrification could erode CNG cylinder demand for passenger vehicles (though commercial vehicles lag). 7) UAE business subdued, regional geopolitical risk (Egypt political/currency risk). 8) Valuation 'cheap' could be justified if cyclical trough, but could also be value trap if cyclical peak and margin reset is structural.
red_flag_reason: 1) Q1 FY27 earnings headwind (-10% rev, -23% EBITDA) warrants near-term caution. 2) Working capital management deteriorated in FY25 (CFO collapse), needs monitoring during growth capex phase. 3) Capex payback periods high (Egypt 18-25y greenfield); ROI depends on execution and market tailwinds materializing. 4) CNG demand cyclicality and competitive threats (Supreme's Type-4) not immaterial. 5) No red flag warranting downgrade to YELLOW beyond normal cycle/execution risk; moat and ROCE suggest fundamentals intact if capex delivers and CNG recovery sustains.

deep_dive.business_summary: Everest Kanto Cylinder (EKC) is India's leading manufacturer of high-pressure seamless gas cylinders with >50% domestic market share, serving industrial gases, medical oxygen, CNG, and emerging clean energy applications (hydrogen, CBG). Established 1978 with 48-year track record. Global footprint: 6 manufacturing facilities across Tarapur, Kandla, Mundra (greenfield), Dubai, Pittsburgh USA, and Egypt (coming online May 2026). Capacity: 1.8M cylinders/year, 30M+ cylinders in service globally.

industry_structure.market_size: Global high-pressure cylinders ~$12B+ annually (8% CAGR to 2036); Type IV hydrogen cylinders $10.6B by 2034 (12.1% CAGR); India CNG tanks $5.5B by 2035 (2.17B in 2025, 10.3% CAGR)
growth_drivers: CNG infrastructure expansion in India (government fuel transition policy)
Hydrogen storage solutions for clean energy transition (global 12.1% CAGR Type IV market)
Semiconductor sector growth in India (ultra-high purity gas needs)
North American CNG conversion for heavy-duty trucks (strong OEM partnerships)
Regional gas adoption in UAE, Egypt, Africa
industry_structure.cyclicality: High: CNG cylinder demand sensitive to fuel pricing at pump (e.g., CNG Rs40->Rs80/kg destroyed CV demand FY23). Industrial cylinders more stable.
industry_structure.concentration: India highly concentrated: EKC ~50%+ market share, 1-2 other competitors (Supreme Industries entering with Type-4, but late-mover). Global: fragmented

earnings_quality.profitability_trends: FY25 PAT flat despite 22.6% revenue growth suggests margin pressure; FY27 Q1 PAT -42% YoY is sharp but Q1 FY26 had Rs 12.6 cr exceptional ERC gain (US tax credit), so adjust: Q1 FY26 operational PAT ~39-40 cr, Q1 FY27 actual 30 cr = -25% organic decline due to temporary headwinds and lower volumes
earnings_quality.fcf_generation: FY25 CFO of Rs 58 cr (down from Rs 226 cr in FY24) due to massive working capital swing (-Rs 97 cr in FY25 vs +Rs 80 cr in FY24), driven by inventory build and receivables surge as US/India volumes ramped. This is a warning sign: growth is consuming working capital.
earnings_quality.asset_quality: Receivables and inventory up sharply; payables management stable. Cash conversion cycle extending. Need to monitor if this is temporary (ramp) or structural (loose credit terms for growth).
earnings_quality.one_off_items: Q1 FY26 had Rs 12.6 cr ERC (exceptional gain). Q1 FY27 had Rs 3.1 cr exceptional loss on labour code provisions. Reported earnings subject to noise.
earnings_quality.accounting_standards: IND AS 116 lease accounting inflates interest and depreciation, depressing reported net margins vs EBITDA. Review EBITDA/PAT margin trends, not just PAT.
earnings_quality.assessment: MEDIUM QUALITY - Solid EBITDA generation and cash flow potential, but working capital management and growth execution (capex timelines) are key risk factors. Recent Q1 weakness is a watch point.

growth_trajectory.historical_5y_revenue_cagr: 9.57% (FY21-FY26, volatility: FY22 spike 79% on CNG super-cycle, FY23 drop to Rs1,274cr post CNG price shock, FY24 flat, FY25 rebound 22.6%)
growth_trajectory.volumes_vs_realizations: FY25: Volumes +18% YoY but realizations fell due to mix and pricing pressure on some contracts. FY27 Q1: Supply constraints limiting volume growth despite demand.

segment_growth.uae_dubai: Subdued, expected to break even in FY27. Revenue likely ~Rs 100-120 cr range, needs improvement.

However, Q1 supply headwinds and working capital drag create near-term caution. FY28+ potential higher if hydrogen and new segments scale.

management_quality.track_record: Pushkar Khurana (Chairman) & Puneet Khurana (MD): Family business since 1978, successfully navigated 2018 allegations (forensic audit never materialized), recovered from FY23 CNG price shock, completed international expansion (US, UAE, Egypt). Operational discipline shown (margin recovery from FY23 lows, ROCE maintained at high levels).
management_quality.capital_allocation: Conservative: Debt reduced over time until recent capex-funded borrowing (Egypt/Mundra). Dividend payout sporadic (4% payout ratio in FY21, nil in recent years while capex ramps). Reinvesting for growth rather than returning to shareholders.
management_quality.execution_proof: Mixed: Egypt facility on track (May 2026 online confirmed), Mundra first line operational, US orders consistent. However, FY25 CFO deterioration due to working capital is a red flag on execution discipline.
management_quality.communication: Management quarterly guidance clear (15-20% FY27 growth, 15-17% EBITDA margin target, Egypt Rs 50-60 cr Y1 revenue). Q3 FY26 concall shows detailed segment understanding and realistic acknowledgment of headwinds (UAE subdued, Egypt ramp-up year).
management_quality.ownership_alignment: Promoters hold significant stake (family business structure), alignment with minority shareholders assumed.
management_quality.assessment: MEDIUM-HIGH - 48-year track record and strong capex execution (Egypt online on time), but recent working capital management and Q1 weakness need monitoring. Credible but not exceptional.

quality_metrics.roce_trend: Strong; 26% ROCE (FY24-FY25 derived from embedded analyses) is well above India average ~12-15%. Historical range: 15-26% depending on cycle.
quality_metrics.net_debt_to_ebitda_trend: Rising due to capex borrowing (Egypt Rs 150 cr, Mundra Rs 100-120 cr), but manageable. Expected to normalize post capex completion (FY27-FY28).
quality_metrics.interest_coverage_notes: Healthy; interest expense only Rs 17-28 cr vs EBITDA Rs 179+ cr. Leverage headroom.
quality_metrics.fcf_conversion_notes: FY25 CFO Rs 58 cr / PAT Rs 98 cr = 59% conversion. FY24 CFO Rs 226 cr / PAT Rs 98 cr = 230% (inflated). 3-year average suggests 60-70% normalized FCF conversion post working capital normalization.
quality_metrics.margin_trend: EBITDA margin: FY21 17%, FY23 low 12%, FY25 12%, FY27 Q1 14%, guidance 15-17%. Trend is recovery but not fully regained FY21 peak. Net margin depressed by IND AS 116 lease accounting.
quality_metrics.capex_efficiency: New capex (Mundra, Egypt, US) targeting high ROI: Egypt first-yr Rs 50-60 cr revenue at likely 12-14% EBITDA margin = Rs 6-8 cr EBITDA on Rs 150 cr capex = payback 18-25 years (high for greenfield, offset by long-term capacity value and regional optionality). US capex USD 5.5 mn (Rs 45 cr) expected to drive Rs 100 cr incremental revenue by FY28 = Rs 20+ cr EBITDA = 2-3 year payback (excellent).
quality_metrics.assessment: HIGH QUALITY - 26% ROCE, strong margins (recovering to 15-17% target), solid interest coverage, capex projects sensible but execution-dependent. Working capital management is the watch point.

track_record.note: FY21-FY25 review: FY22 exceptional year (FY22 exceptional ERC gain masked true operational EBITDA), FY23-24 cyclical trough (CNG price shock), FY25 recovery. ROCE sustained at 15-26% range throughout, suggesting durable competitive position. No accounting scandals post-2018 allegations investigation. Execution on international expansion (US turnaround, Egypt greenfield, UAE maintained) shows operational competence despite cyclical headwinds. Verdict: Credible operator with proven ability to navigate cycles.

four_box.note: REVISED 2026-10-05 DEEPDIVE: (1) Tailwind: CNG infra expansion, hydrogen adoption (12.1% CAGR global Type IV market), clean energy transition globally are real multi-year themes; India alone targeting CNG in 10+ states, government push on fuel transition = Moderate (not weak). (2) TAM: Global high-pressure cylinders ~$12B, Type IV hydrogen $10.6B by 2034, India CNG $5.5B by 2035; Egypt/Africa regional expansion adds optionality; US CNG heavy-truck conversion is large and growing = Moderate (not weak). (3) Moat: >50% India market share, 48-year legacy, 30M+ cylinders installed base (switching costs), technical/regulatory barriers (PESO approval, high-pressure expertise), entry into higher-margin segments (semiconductors, defence, Type-4) = Moderate-Strong (not weak). P/E 8.9x is cheap for a 26% ROCE business. (4) Valuation: Yes. VERDICT: 10x-in-3-5-years thesis upgraded to MEDIUM conviction; score 3.0 supports larger thesis vs initial 2.5. Risk: execution on capex (Egypt/Mundra timelines), cyclical CNG demand, working capital drag during growth, competitive threats (Supreme's Type-4).

four_box_metadata.methodology: User framework: growth+margins+ROCE+debt+capex+FCF+moat+mgmt quality; bet on rerating of good businesses. Four-box is mechanical gate. Score 3.0 (moderate-strong thesis) permits 10x/100x targets.
conviction_drivers: P/E 8.9x (valuation discount justified if cyclical trough, risky if cyclical peak)
Management execution credible but working capital / capex delivery is watch

Thesis: Mundra+Egypt+US capex + CNG recovery + margin climb to 15-17% = 10-15% revenue CAGR over 3-5 years, multiple re-rating from 8.9x to 12-15x = 3-4x price upside, combines to 10x scenario if PAT CAGR 18% (historical) sustained and multiple expands 2x.

deep_dive_metadata.confidence_level: High (official NSE/BSE results, mgmt concall, peer research, market data)

conviction_rationale: Four-box score 3.0 (up from 2.5) supports 10x/100x thesis. Moat/tailwind/TAM upgraded from weak to moderate/moderate-strong on deepdive. Management execution proven (Egypt online track record, US turnaround, Mundra ramp), but Q1 FY27 weakness and working capital drain warrant caution. ROCE 26% is exceptional; valuation 8.9x P/E is deeply discounted. Bull case: Multiple re-rating (8.9x -> 12-15x) + PAT CAGR 10-15% + capex payoff = 10x in 3-5 years. Bear case: Cyclical trough overblown, CNG demand weak, capex delays, WC drain persists. MEDIUM reflects balanced risk/reward with proven moat but execution-dependent upside.

track_record.note: FY21-FY25 review completed. ROCE sustained 15-26% throughout cycle = durable moat. No accounting scandals post-2018 investigation. Execution on international expansion (US turnaround, Egypt greenfield planning, UAE maintained) credible. FY23-24 cyclical trough survived, FY25 recovery achieved. Verdict: Credible operator with proven ability to navigate cycles, but working capital and capex execution are key monitoring points.
